results.source: XPACE technical report, Figure 7 and Section 4.3.1, page 16
notes: Original figure rounds average success-rate bar labels to 7 and 68; the page 16 results prose explicitly reports 6.7% and 68.3%.
Progress values are transcribed from displayed labels rather than reconstructed averages.
results.title: Real-robot benchmark
results.caption: Figure 7 · Banana pick-and-place, water pouring, and bowl stacking; 20 trials per task per method. Average success rates follow the report text (6.7% and 68.3%); the original figure rounds them to 7% and 68%. Progress averages are retained as reported. Only XPACE receives Stage I video adaptation; this compares complete systems.

robustness.source: XPACE technical report, Figure 8, page 16; explanatory text page 17
notes: 20 trials per task. Robot-only removes human data and unsupervised video, so this is a combined data ablation.
robustness.title: Position and distractor robustness
robustness.caption: Figure 8 · Position and distractor robustness, with 20 real-robot trials per task. The robot-only variant excludes human data and unsupervised video.

improvement.source: XPACE technical report, Figure 12, page 20; Section 4.3.6 text page 21
notes: This suite uses cola handover rather than bowl stacking; do not conflate with main results average.
Before DAgger banana and pour values reuse the main experiment trials.
Progress values are transcribed from displayed labels rather than reconstructed averages.
improvement.title: Policy improvement
improvement.caption: Figure 12 · Banana pick-and-place, water pouring, and cola handover; 20 trials per task per method. Shaded columns show unweighted task averages. Before DAgger results for banana pick-and-place and water pouring reuse the Figure 7 trials. This suite replaces bowl stacking with cola handover; the comparison includes the additional fine-tuning budget.

pretraining.source: XPACE technical report, Figure 10 and Section 4.3.3, page 18
notes: Zero exposure retains the pretrained video-DiT initialization but receives no Stage I adaptation.
All arms use matched supervised action fine-tuning and the same action-head initialization seed. Values are tail-window averages.
Exposure checkpoints use equally spaced categories, matching Figure 10; exposure and Stage I optimization compute increase together.
Line color #0068b8 sampled from the PDF-rendered Figure 10; Figure 11 uses the report’s #dfc985 and #6086b0 bars.
pretraining.title: Video pretraining prepares the policy for control
pretraining.caption: Figure 10 · Teacher-forced action-loss change relative to no Stage I adaptation, after matched action fine-tuning (tail-window average; MSE in normalized action space). Lower is better. Stage I exposure and pretraining compute increase together.

coverage.source: XPACE technical report, Figure 11, page 20; Section 4.3.5, page 19
notes: Rows follow Figure 11 from top to bottom: robot-dense/human-dense; robot-absent/human-dense; robot-absent/human-sparse; robot-absent/human-absent.
Values and the yellow/blue series assignment were visually audited against Figure 11.
Positive values mean lower action loss than robot-only; negative values mean higher loss.
Means over nine late-training checkpoints; coverage strata are secondary semantic groupings, not original dataset partitions.
coverage.title: Human experience across task-coverage strata
coverage.caption: Figure 11 · Action-loss reduction relative to robot-only, averaged over nine late-training checkpoints. Positive values mean lower loss; negative values mean higher loss. Coverage describes each task family in the robot and human training corpora.
